content.title: About
content.content: Paella is a traditional Spanish dish originating from Valencia. Its base is short‑grain rice (such as Arborio or Bomba) cooked in a wide, shallow pan (paellera) with broth, olive oil, saffron, and a variety of add‑ins: seafood, chicken, rabbit, vegetables, and chorizo sausage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional paella is cooked over an open fire using charcoal for a distinctive smoky flavor.
Saffron, which gives the dish its golden hue, is one of the most expensive spices in the world.
There are several regional versions: seafood paella, Valencian paella (chicken and rabbit), and mixed paella (meat and seafood).
The rice is not stirred during cooking, allowing a crispy crust called “socarrat” to form on the bottom.
Paella has become a symbol of Spanish cuisine and is often served at festivals and family celebrations.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides sustained energy and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Complete protein from meat and seafood
items.content: Chicken, rabbit, seafood, and chorizo supply all essential amino acids.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil adds monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Saffron, vegetables, and seafood contribute vitamin C, B‑vitamins, iron, and magnesium.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Saffron and olive oil are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People allergic to shellfish or fish may react to seafood paella.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Broths and cured meats can increase the dish’s salt level.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Generous amounts of oil and sausage raise the calorie count.

items.title: Heavy‑metal exposure
items.content: Some seafood may contain trace amounts of cadmium or mercury; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve paella hot straight from the pan. Eat with a fork or spoon, optionally squeezing fresh lemon juice over it. Garnish with chopped parsley or basil and a light side salad if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth or water to restore moisture. Paella can be frozen for up to 2 months.
